findings.label: Prominent eyes
findings.evidence: face photography of an infant with Marshall Smith syndrome showing signs of craniofacial dysmorphism including prominent eyes

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: The panel clearly displays craniofacial dysmorphism (prominent eyes, upturned nares, prominent forehead) consistent with Marshall-Smith Syndrome in an infant. B: Anterior segment photography shows severe ocular pathology (corneal edema and total cataract) reported in a case of Marshall-Smith Syndrome. C: Shows corneal scarring secondary to hydrops, a specific complication of ocular involvement in this patient with Marshall-Smith Syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Sayadi and Malek. Congenital cataract and congenital glaucoma in Marshall-Smith syndrome.. The Pan African medical journal 2021. doi:10.11604/pamj.2021.40.147.30762. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
